name: Four Seasons Resort AMAALA at Triple Bay
insider_take: This ultra-luxury resort sits on Saudi Arabia's pristine Red Sea coastline, where untouched coral reefs meet dramatic desert landscapes in one of the world's most ambitious eco-tourism destinations.
whats_special: Four Seasons Resort AMAALA is part of Saudi Arabia's groundbreaking NEOM megaproject, featuring overwater villas and beachfront suites designed to blend seamlessly with the natural environment. The resort offers direct access to some of the Red Sea's most pristine coral reefs, with water so clear you can see 30 meters down. The property is powered entirely by renewable energy and built using sustainable materials sourced locally.
pro_tip: Book diving excursions during the cooler months (October-April) when visibility is at its peak and you'll encounter whale sharks, manta rays, and over 1,200 species of fish in waters that remain largely unexplored by mass tourism.
dont_miss: The resort's signature spa treatments using locally-sourced Dead Sea minerals, sunset camel treks across the nearby Tabuk mountains, and snorkeling at the untouched Sheybarah Island where sea turtles nest. The property's stargazing experiences are exceptional thanks to minimal light pollution in this remote location.
pros: Pristine Red Sea Access – Situated along Saudi Arabia's unspoiled Red Sea coastline, guests enjoy direct access to crystal-clear waters and world-class coral reefs ideal for snorkeling and diving.
Ultra-Luxury Four Seasons Signature Service – Renowned Five-Star hospitality with impeccable, personalized service throughout every aspect of the stay.
Wellness & Spa Excellence – A dedicated world-class wellness destination featuring extensive spa facilities, holistic treatments, and curated well-being programming.
Exclusive Destination Within AMAALA – Part of Saudi Arabia's visionary giga-project, offering a rare and exclusive travel experience at one of the world's most anticipated luxury destinations.
Stunning Architectural Design – Thoughtfully designed interiors and architecture that harmonize with the natural desert and coastal landscape for a truly immersive environment.
cons: Remote, Secluded Location – The resort's pristine setting along Saudi Arabia's northwest coast means limited nearby off-resort dining, shopping, or cultural attractions.
Newly Opened Destination – As part of an emerging mega-development, surrounding infrastructure and destination amenities are still evolving.
Ultra-Premium Price Point – The exceptional level of luxury and exclusivity comes with a significant investment, positioning this resort for the most discerning luxury travelers.
